name: Coal Road Dispersed Primitive Camping - George Washington & Jefferson National Forests

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Glenwood-Pedlar Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for general forest dispersed camping
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted along Forest Service Road 162 (Coal Road). Campsites set back 100ft from St. Mary's Wilderness boundary and streams.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6-8 inches deep in organic soil, 200 feet from St. Mary's River. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out. Black bears active: bear canister or vehicle storage mandatory.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only within forest.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established rock fire rings only. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Virginia Department of Forestry burn bans during spring (Feb-April 4 PM rule) and autumn.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved gravel forest service road (FS 162 / Coal Road)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Washboard gravel forest road with small potholes and dips.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (easily accessible along main Coal Road gravel turnouts in dry weather)

nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low to Moderate (Blue Ridge Mountain foothill valley)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 55-70°F, blooming mountain laurel, high waterfall flow in St. Mary's gorge.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: 78-86°F, shaded oak canopy, mountain river swimming holes.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Spectacular Blue Ridge autumn foliage (55-70°F daytime, 35-45°F nights), prime camping.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cool 35-50°F, freezing night temperatures, light snow dustings.

dangers_and_hazards: Black Bears active throughout GWNF - store food securely
Copperheads and Timber Rattlesnakes near rocky outcrops
Flash flooding along St. Mary's River after heavy rain

common_human_made_sounds: Occasional camper vehicle on Coal Road

human_demographics_and_culture: St. Mary's Wilderness backpackers, Blue Ridge Parkway travelers, digital nomads, and local trout anglers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Monacan indigenous traditions revere the Blue Ridge Mountains and Shenandoah river valleys as sacred spirit vision lands.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Blue Ridge quartzite mountain energy, crystal-clear stream acoustics, fast 5G connectivity.

nearby_hiking_trails.trail_name: St. Mary's Waterfall Trail (St. Mary's Wilderness)
nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding stream trail leading to 15-foot waterfall swimming hole

public_reviews_summary: Top choice for free primitive camping in Virginia. Easy road access, beautiful Blue Ridge Mountain setting, and fast 5G cell internet.
other_data: Bortle Class 3 night sky. Abundant firewood.
